analysis.plain_explanation: You paid a large amount of Rs 60 lakh to a luxury car dealer who failed to deliver the car and is refusing to refund your money. Since the amount paid is above Rs 50 lakh, your case falls under the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission rather than the District Commission. You have multiple legal routes available, including filing a consumer complaint for deficiency in service or unfair trade practice, or pursuing a civil claim for recovery of money. However, since the delay is significant, you should act promptly and consult a lawyer to calculate exact limitation timelines and choose the best forum.

steps.title: Send a formal legal notice
steps.detail: Send a formal legal notice to the luxury car dealer demanding the delivery of the vehicle or a full refund of Rs 60 lakh along with appropriate compensation and interest.
steps.where: By registered post or email to the car dealer's official business address.

steps.title: (General) Register a complaint on the National Consumer Helpline
steps.detail: Register your grievance regarding non-delivery and refusal of refund through the National Consumer Helpline portal or by calling 1915.

steps.title: File a consumer complaint at the State Consumer Commission
steps.detail: Since the amount paid is above Rs 50 lakh up to Rs 2 crore, file a formal consumer complaint for deficiency in service and unfair trade practice at the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.
steps.where: State Consumer Commission (via e-Jagriti portal or physically)

steps.title: Consult a legal professional for civil or criminal recovery options
steps.detail: Consult a lawyer to review limitation timelines under the Sale of Goods Act, 1930 and evaluate whether to pursue a civil recovery suit or criminal complaint for cheating if dishonest intent is established.
steps.where: Local advocate or District Legal Services Authority (DLSA / NALSA 15100) for legal guidance

draft_document.text:
To,
[LUXURY CAR DEALER NAME]
[DEALER ADDRESS]

SUBJECT: LEGAL NOTICE FOR REFUND OF RS 60 LAKH AND COMPENSATION FOR NON-DELIVERY OF VEHICLE

Dear Sir/Madam,

I, [YOUR NAME], resident of [YOUR ADDRESS], state the following:

1. That in January 2026, I paid a sum of Rs 60,00,000 (Rupees Sixty Lakhs only) to your dealership for the purchase of a luxury car, as evidenced by the booking agreement and payment proof dated [DATE OF PAYMENT].
2. That despite the lapse of several months, you have failed to deliver the vehicle as promised, which amounts to a serious deficiency in service and an unfair trade practice.
3. That my repeated emails and requests for delivery or a full refund have been ignored or refused by your establishment.

Therefore, through this legal notice, I call upon you to refund the entire amount of Rs 60,00,000 along with appropriate interest and compensation within 15 days of receiving this notice. Failing this, I shall be constrained to initiate legal proceedings against you before the appropriate State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission and other forums as per law, at your sole risk and cost.

Sincerely,
[YOUR NAME]
[YOUR CONTACT INFORMATION]
[DATE]

reasons: The amount is above Rs 50 lakh, which is beyond the District Consumer Commission. A lawyer is strongly advised.
